stories.title: BSUID: migrate contact identity to Business-Scoped User ID by June 2026
stories.description: WhatsApp is launching usernames in June 2026, after which users' phone numbers may no longer be available in webhook payloads. Meta will deliver a per-business BSUID in all webhook `from`/`to` fields. Rainbow AI must capture and persist BSUIDs alongside phone numbers so conversations, history lookups, and CRM records do not break when phone numbers become optional.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming webhook parser reads the `user_id` / BSUID field and stores it alongside the phone number in `rainbow_conversations`
Contact lookup falls back to BSUID when phone number is absent from the webhook payload
Existing conversations keyed by phone number are not broken during the transition period
A migration script maps existing phone-number-keyed rows to their BSUIDs once Meta starts delivering them
Unit test: webhook with only BSUID (no phone number) is processed correctly and conversation continues
technicalNotes: BSUID delivered in webhook `user_id` field from June 2026
Phone numbers remain available for 30 days after any prior interaction, then may be absent
Store both identifiers; BSUID is unique per-business so no cross-tenant collision risk
Ref: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-usernames--new-business-scoped-user-id--bsuid--field-re

stories.title: Enforce WhatsApp business-purpose-only AI policy (no general-purpose assistant mode)
stories.description: Since January 15 2026 Meta bans general-purpose AI assistants on the WhatsApp Business Platform. Bots must serve a specific business purpose. Rainbow AI must technically enforce that every response is scoped to hostel/cafe operations, blocking open-ended assistant queries to avoid Terms of Service violation and potential account suspension.
acceptanceCriteria: System prompt explicitly defines allowed intents: bookings, check-in/out, F&B orders, hostel info, cafe menu — no open-ended assistant mode
Intent classifier rejects off-scope requests (e.g. 'write me a poem', 'explain quantum physics') with a polite redirect to business topics
Off-scope rate logged in intent_analytics for compliance audit trail
Admin panel shows a 'Compliance Mode' toggle and logs any manual overrides
Test: off-scope query returns redirect message, not a general AI answer
technicalNotes: Meta WhatsApp Business Solution Terms updated October 2025; violation triggers account review
AI Providers (general-purpose LLM resale) are explicitly prohibited; task-specific bots are allowed
Implement an off-scope guard layer before the main LLM call in the pipeline
Ref: https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/18/whatssapp-changes-its-terms-to-bar-general-purpose-chatbots-from-its-platform/

stories.title: Express CVE-2024-51999: patch query parser prototype pollution vulnerability
stories.description: CVE-2024-51999 (disclosed December 2025) is a prototype pollution vulnerability in Express's query-string parser. If the extended query parser is enabled, an attacker can inject prototype-polluting keys via URL query parameters, potentially altering global object behaviour. Rainbow AI's admin API endpoints accept query parameters and must be patched.
acceptanceCriteria: Express version is updated to the patched release that addresses CVE-2024-51999
If the extended query parser is used, it is replaced with `qs` configured with `plainObjects: true`
`npm audit` reports zero high/critical vulnerabilities after the fix
All query-parameter handling in admin routes is tested with prototype-polluting payloads (e.g. `?__proto__[admin]=true`)
A Dependabot or Snyk alert rule is configured to auto-raise PRs for future Express CVEs
technicalNotes: CVE-2024-51999: affects Express `req.query` when extended parser is active; attacker modifies `Object.prototype` properties via crafted query string
Fix: use `qs.parse(str, { plainObjects: true })` or upgrade to patched Express version
Ref: https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-EXPRESS-14157151

stories.title: npm supply chain: pin dependency versions and enable integrity verification
stories.description: In September 2025 a major npm supply-chain attack compromised 18 widely-used packages including chalk and debug via maintainer account phishing. CISA issued an advisory. Rainbow AI's `package.json` uses semver ranges, allowing malicious patch-level updates to auto-install. Exact version pinning and package-lock integrity enforcement must be applied.
acceptanceCriteria: All direct dependencies in `package.json` use exact version pins (no `^` or `~` prefixes)
`package-lock.json` is committed to the repository and CI fails if it is out of sync
CI pipeline runs `npm audit --audit-level=high` and fails on high/critical findings
A Dependabot or Renovate configuration is added that reviews version bumps via PR rather than auto-merging
Developer npm accounts used in CI have phishing-resistant MFA (hardware key or passkey) enabled
technicalNotes: CISA advisory September 23 2025: widespread supply-chain compromise impacting npm ecosystem
Affected packages: chalk, debug, ansi-styles, strip-ansi — common transitive deps
Use `npm ci` (not `npm install`) in CI for reproducible installs from lockfile
Ref: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/09/23/widespread-supply-chain-compromise-impacting-npm-ecosystem

stories.title: On-Premises API sunset: audit and remove all on-premises API references from codebase
stories.description: The WhatsApp On-Premises API expired on October 23 2025 and can no longer send messages. Any infrastructure referencing the on-premises client Docker image or on-premises endpoints must be audited and removed. A migration plan to official Cloud API should be documented as the canonical future path.
acceptanceCriteria: Codebase and Docker configs contain no references to the WhatsApp on-premises API Docker image or on-premises endpoints
Documentation clearly states that Baileys (direct WebSocket) is used and flags the compliance/TOS risk vs. official Cloud API
A migration plan exists for moving from Baileys to official Cloud API, with effort estimate, in the architecture docs
If Cloud API is already used alongside Baileys, the integration is tested end-to-end to confirm on-premises client is not referenced
technicalNotes: On-premises sunset confirmed October 23 2025: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/on-premises/sunset
Baileys is a reverse-engineered client — not subject to on-premises sunset but carries different TOS risk
Cloud API migration would require BSP (Business Solution Provider) or direct Meta account

stories.title: WhatsApp 100K messaging tier: monitor daily volume limits and surface upgrade eligibility
stories.description: Meta is removing the graduated 2K to 100K messaging tier steps in Q2 2026, letting verified businesses jump directly to 100K/day. Rainbow AI's admin panel should show current tier, daily message count against the limit, and alert when approaching the cap so operators can proactively qualify and avoid dropped messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows current messaging tier (1K / 10K / 100K / unlimited) and messages sent today vs. the tier limit
Alert fires at 80% and 95% of the daily tier limit
When daily limit is hit, outgoing message queue pauses gracefully and logs which messages were delayed
Admin panel links to the Meta Business Manager page to initiate tier upgrade
Tier history is logged so operators can demonstrate growth trajectory to Meta
technicalNotes: Tier eligibility: phone number quality rating must be 'High' or 'Medium'; no policy violations in last 30 days
Meta Q2 2026: selected partners get direct access to 100K tier without stepping through intermediate tiers
Current tier level available via GET /v21.0/{phone-number-id} `messaging_limit_tier` field
Ref: https://sanuker.com/whatsapp-api-2026_updates-pacing-limits-usernames/

stories.title: OWASP LLM03:2025 — AI model supply chain integrity verification
stories.description: OWASP LLM03:2025 (a new entry in the 2025 revision of the Top 10) identifies supply-chain risks in AI model providers including compromised model weights and third-party API manipulation. Rainbow AI uses NVIDIA Kimi K2.5, OpenRouter, and Ollama. The system must verify provider behaviour and detect unexpected output changes that may indicate supply-chain compromise.
acceptanceCriteria: Model provider responses are validated against expected output format and refusal patterns to detect anomalous behaviour
A canary prompt suite (fixed questions with known expected outputs) runs on every deployment and on a daily schedule; deviations alert the operator
All API calls to AI providers include model version pinning where the API supports it
A SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) entry exists for each AI provider dependency
Ollama local model is pre-tested as a verified fallback in case upstream provider compromise is suspected
technicalNotes: LLM03:2025 explicitly covers Hugging Face LoRA/PEFT supply-chain poisoning and account compromise vectors
Anomaly detection: compare provider response style/structure over time; major drift signals possible tampering
Ref: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/

stories.title: Malaysia PDPA 2025: Transfer Impact Assessment for cross-border data flows to AI providers
stories.description: The Malaysia PDPA Cross-Border Personal Data Transfer Guidelines (effective April 29 2025) require a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) before sending personal data outside Malaysia. Rainbow AI sends guest data to NVIDIA/OpenRouter (US-based) and Neon PostgreSQL (US). A TIA must be documented for each processor and reviewed every 3 years.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented TIA exists for each third-party data processor receiving Malaysian guest personal data (NVIDIA API, OpenRouter, Neon, AWS)
TIA covers: destination country legal framework, enforcement mechanisms, security standards, potential government access
Transfer records include receiver name, country, data type, and purpose in `rainbow_config_audit`
TIA is reviewed and re-filed every 3 years (automated calendar reminder in admin panel)
Privacy notice updated to disclose cross-border transfer destinations and legal basis
technicalNotes: PDPA Section 129 and CBPDT Guidelines: mandatory record-keeping of receiver name, registration number, DPO contact, country, data type, purpose
Condition 1B: destination must provide 'adequate level of protection equivalent to PDPA' — US providers typically rely on contractual safeguards
Guidelines: https://www.pdp.gov.my/ppdpv1/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/GP_CBPDT_EN-1.pdf

stories.title: Malaysia PDPA 2025: data breach notification within 72-hour statutory window
stories.description: Phase 3 PDPA amendments (June 1 2025) impose mandatory breach notification: data controllers must notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach. Rainbow AI stores guest PII and must have an automated detection and notification workflow that meets these statutory deadlines or face fines up to RM 1,000,000.
acceptanceCriteria: Automated monitoring detects anomalous bulk data reads/exports and triggers an internal alert within 1 hour
An incident response runbook documents the 72-hour notification process to the PDPC
Admin panel has a 'Report Data Breach' workflow that pre-fills the statutory notification form with affected record counts, data types, and probable cause
Breach events are persisted with timestamp, scope, and response actions taken
Tabletop exercise confirms the 72-hour SLA is achievable with the runbook
technicalNotes: PDPA (Amendment) Act 2024 s.12A: notification 'as soon as practicable' — guideline sets 72 hours as the hard deadline
Maximum fine raised to RM 1,000,000 and up to 3 years imprisonment for non-compliance
PDPC portal for breach registration: https://spdp.pdp.gov.my
Ref: https://privacymatters.dlapiper.com/2025/03/malaysia-guidelines-issued-on-data-breach-notification-and-data-protection-officer-appointment/

stories.title: Webhook idempotency: deduplicate WhatsApp message deliveries using Redis key store
stories.description: WhatsApp Cloud API retries webhook deliveries when your endpoint does not respond within ~10 seconds or returns a non-2xx status. Without idempotency guards, the same guest message can be processed twice, generating duplicate AI replies, double-charges, or duplicate booking records. A Redis-backed deduplication layer using the message ID as the key eliminates this class of bug.
acceptanceCriteria: Each incoming webhook event is checked against a Redis key `whatsapp:msg:{messageId}` before processing
If the key exists, the event is silently acknowledged (HTTP 200) and dropped
If the key does not exist, it is set with a 6-hour TTL before processing begins
HTTP 200 is returned to WhatsApp within 2 seconds; processing continues asynchronously
Integration test: send the same webhook payload twice in rapid succession; confirm only one AI reply is sent
technicalNotes: WhatsApp webhook timeout is 10 seconds; Meta retries on failure with exponential backoff
Use `messages[].id` for inbound messages and `statuses[].id` for delivery status deduplication
Job queue: Bull/BullMQ backed by Redis is a natural complement to the dedup store
Ref: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 / ARIA: implement role=log live region for screen reader accessibility in webchat widget
stories.description: The Rainbow AI webchat widget has no ARIA live region support. Screen reader users receive no announcement when the AI responds. WCAG best practices require the chat message list to use `role='log'` so assistive technologies announce new messages as they arrive, and the input area must be properly labelled.
acceptanceCriteria: The chat message list container has `role='log'` and `aria-label='Conversation history'`
New messages appended to the log are announced by screen readers via the implicit `aria-live='polite'` of `role='log'`
The chat input field has a visible label or `aria-label='Type your message'`
The send button has `aria-label='Send message'`
The live region is present in the initial DOM (empty) before any content is injected to ensure accessibility API registration
Tested with NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari: new AI messages are announced without interrupting the user
technicalNotes: Use `role='log'` (implicit `aria-live='polite'`, `aria-atomic='false'`) for chat history — not `aria-live='assertive'` which interrupts
Live region must be present in initial DOM (empty) before any content is injected
W3C ARIA technique ARIA23: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/aria/ARIA23
Ref: https://a11y-guidelines.orange.com/en/articles/chatbot/

stories.title: WhatsApp pricing analytics: cost-per-conversation breakdown by intent category
stories.description: With per-message pricing in effect since July 2025, certain high-frequency intents may generate disproportionate costs. The admin dashboard should break down messaging costs by intent category so operators can identify expensive flows and optimise them (e.g. route to free utility window, batch replies).
acceptanceCriteria: Each outgoing message's cost data from the `pricing` webhook field is joined to its conversation's detected intent
Dashboard shows top-10 most expensive intents by total monthly spend
Cost-per-resolved-conversation metric is available per intent
Operator can set a per-intent cost alert threshold
Historical cost data is retained for 90 days minimum
technicalNotes: Meta pricing webhook: `statuses[].pricing.billable` (bool), `.pricing_model` ('CBP' or 'PMP'), `.pricing.category`
Join pricing data to `rainbow_messages.intent` column in analytics queries
Ref: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing/updates-to-pricing/

stories.title: Multi-agent inbox: assign and hand off conversations between Rainbow AI and human agents
stories.description: Currently Rainbow AI handles all conversations autonomously; staff cannot interject or claim a conversation without the guest re-initiating. A human-takeover and reassignment flow is needed for complex or escalated cases, allowing staff to view the live queue, claim a conversation, respond manually, and return it to AI mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Staff can view a live queue of active AI-handled conversations in the admin panel
A 'Take over' button pauses AI auto-replies for that conversation and assigns it to the staff member
The guest receives a seamless transition message (e.g. 'You are now speaking with our team.')
Staff can return the conversation to AI mode after resolving the issue
Escalation events are logged in `escalation_events` with agent ID, timestamp, and reason
Conversation assignment is visible to all online agents to avoid double-handling
technicalNotes: WhatsApp Business API allows unlimited agents via third-party platforms
Implement conversation state machine: AI_ACTIVE -> ESCALATED -> HUMAN_ACTIVE -> RESOLVED / AI_ACTIVE
Admin panel WebSocket push for real-time queue updates without polling
Ref: https://respond.io/whatsapp-business-multiple-users

stories.title: Malaysia PDPA 2025: Transfer Impact Assessment record-keeping module in admin panel
stories.description: The CBPDT Guidelines require data controllers to maintain records of every cross-border personal data transfer including receiver details, country, data type, and purpose. These records must be producible on demand by the PDPC. Rainbow AI's admin panel needs a Transfer Records module to create and maintain these statutory records.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin panel has a 'Data Transfer Records' section listing each third-party processor (NVIDIA, OpenRouter, Neon, AWS Lightsail)
Each record includes: receiver name, registration/company number, receiver DPO contact, destination country, personal data categories transferred, purpose, legal basis, TIA date, TIA review due date
Records are exportable as PDF/CSV for regulator submission
System warns operator 60 days before a TIA review is due (3-year expiry)
Audit log records who created or modified each transfer record and when
technicalNotes: PDPA CBPDT Guidelines s.14: mandatory record fields specified
Records must be retained for the duration of the transfer plus a reasonable period post-cessation
Guideline PDF: https://www.pdp.gov.my/ppdpv1/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/GP_CBPDT_EN-1.pdf

stories.title: ISO 42001 AIMS: document AI system scope, risk register, and incident log
stories.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the international AI Management System standard becoming the benchmark for responsible AI deployment. Prisma Technology deploying Rainbow AI to hospitality clients should maintain the minimum ISO 42001 artefacts: an AI system scope statement, a risk register, and an incident log for AI-related failures.
acceptanceCriteria: An AI System Scope document exists defining: what Rainbow AI does, what it does not do, affected parties (guests, staff), and deployment context
An AI Risk Register lists at least: hallucination risk, PII leakage risk, provider dependency risk, and language/cultural bias risk (BM/EN/ZH)
Every AI-related incident (wrong answer, data leak, service outage) is logged in `rainbow_config_audit` with a root-cause and corrective action
The risk register is reviewed quarterly by a named responsible person
A responsible AI statement is published in the admin panel and referenced in the guest privacy notice
technicalNotes: ISO 42001 Clause 6.1: AI risk assessment; Clause 9.1: monitoring and measurement; Clause 10.2: nonconformity and corrective action
Malaysia's AI Governance & Ethics Guidelines (Sept 2024) align with ISO 42001
Ref: https://www.iso.org/standard/42001

stories.title: NIST AI RMF: implement plain-language explainability for AI-initiated decisions shown to guests
stories.description: NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, July 2024) identifies Explainable AI as a core trustworthiness characteristic. When Rainbow AI escalates a conversation, declines a request, or makes a recommendation, guests should receive a plain-language explanation of why rather than an opaque AI decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Every AI-initiated escalation includes a brief reason shown to both guest and agent (e.g. 'Transferred to staff: your request involves a special arrangement.')
When Rainbow AI cannot fulfil a request, the reply includes a reason category (e.g. 'outside operating hours', 'requires manual confirmation') not a generic sorry message
Admin panel shows per-conversation decision traces: intent classified, confidence score, action taken, reason
Test: for each major intent type, confirm the guest reply contains an explainability phrase
technicalNotes: NIST AI 600-1 Gen AI Profile: 12 specific GenAI risks including lack of transparency and unexplainable outputs
NIST AI RMF GOVERN function: document AI decision logic; MAP function: identify where unexplainability harms users
Ref: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf

stories.title: Malaysia AI Governance 2024: fairness and cultural bias audit for BM/EN/ZH responses
stories.description: Malaysia's National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics (September 2024) require AI systems to address fairness and harmful bias. Rainbow AI serves guests in Bahasa Malaysia, English, and Chinese. Response quality, helpfulness, and tone must be audited across all three languages to ensure no demographic group receives inferior service.
acceptanceCriteria: A test suite of 30+ representative guest queries exists in BM, EN, and ZH covering all major intents
Response quality scoring (helpfulness, accuracy, tone) is evaluated across all three language variants
No intent shows more than 15% quality gap between languages
Cultural sensitivity review: responses in BM include appropriate Malay honorifics; responses in ZH use Malaysian Chinese conventions
Bias audit results are documented and reviewed quarterly
technicalNotes: Malaysia AI Governance & Ethics 7 principles include: fairness, inclusiveness, transparency
Use Promptfoo (already in the project) for multilingual evaluation across language variants
Ref: https://fpf.org/blog/malaysia-charts-its-digital-course-a-guide-to-the-new-frameworks-for-data-protection-and-ai-ethics/

stories.title: MM Lite API integration for AI-optimised marketing broadcast delivery
stories.description: Meta's Marketing Messages Lite (MM Lite) API uses Meta's ad-serving prioritisation logic to achieve up to 9% higher delivery rates than standard Cloud API for marketing templates. For Rainbow AI's hostel/cafe broadcast campaigns (room promotions, menu specials), adopting MM Lite reduces undelivered messages and improves open rates without requiring template changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The broadcast campaign sender in the admin panel has an option to use MM Lite API endpoint instead of standard Cloud API for marketing templates
MM Lite is not used for utility or authentication messages (correct category enforcement)
Delivery analytics compare MM Lite vs. standard API delivery rates over a 30-day period
Portfolio pacing is delegated to Meta when using MM Lite sends
Fallback to standard Cloud API if MM Lite endpoint returns an error
technicalNotes: MM Lite uses the same approved marketing templates; no template re-approval needed
API endpoint differs from standard Cloud API; requires separate send path in the broadcast module
Verify MY market availability before enabling — currently expanding beyond India
Ref: https://www.infobip.com/docs/whatsapp/mm-lite

stories.title: NIST AI RMF GOVERN: publish AI Acceptable Use Policy for hostel/cafe operator context
stories.description: NIST AI RMF's GOVERN function requires organisations to establish policies and accountability structures for AI use. Currently Rainbow AI has no published Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) governing how staff may configure it, what guest data it may process, and what actions it must not take. This AUP protects Prisma Technology commercially and sets clear operator boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: A one-page AI Acceptable Use Policy is published in the admin panel under Settings > Compliance
AUP defines: permitted uses (bookings, menu queries, hostel FAQs), prohibited uses (medical/legal advice, financial commitments), and data handling constraints
Staff onboarding flow includes acknowledgement of the AUP
AUP is version-controlled with a change log
Privacy notice presented to guests references the AUP URL
technicalNotes: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1: policies, processes, procedures for AI risk management are established
AUP also mitigates OWASP LLM08 (excessive agency) by defining operational boundaries in human-readable form
Ref: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/nist.ai.100-1.pdf
